title: A sideways photon in a moving detector frame
promptMarkdown: A photon has energy $E$ and travels along $+y$ in S. S\prime moves at $3c/5$ along $+x$. Compute all components of $P\prime$, its energy and direction, and verify the null norm. Derive the general formula for $\cos\theta\prime$ for a photon initially at angle $\theta$ to $+x$. Explain why no photon rest frame appears even when its energy changes.
hintLadder: Transform the energy and x momentum together; y momentum stays fixed.
Direction cosines are momentum components divided by $E\prime/c$.
Test whether a finite invertible transformation can send a nonzero vector to zero.
